findings.exact_quote: money, a badge, a business, a secret that could end more than just a crush
findings.explanation: An innocent Chuck mentions 'a badge', which points to Pete's hidden undercover-cop identity. Chuck has no way to know it; his rumor about Pete only says he might be hiding something.
findings.suggested_replacement: money, a reputation, a business, a secret that could end more than just a crush

findings.exact_quote: feeling like a informant instead of a friend
findings.explanation: Wrong article: 'a' before a vowel sound. It should be 'an informant'.
findings.suggested_replacement: feeling like an informant instead of a friend

findings.exact_quote: slip something into a man's drink
findings.explanation: The victim Dusty is gender-neutral in the package, so calling Dusty 'a man' breaks the convention.
findings.suggested_replacement: slip something into Dusty's drink

findings.exact_quote: that policy he never told anyone about doesn't sit right with me
findings.explanation: Sandro's life insurance policy on Dusty is his hidden secret. Gio's own secret only covers Sandro's debts, so an innocent Gio cannot know about the policy.
findings.suggested_replacement: and the way he's been so calm about losing Dusty doesn't sit right with me

findings.exact_quote: while the poison worked its way through the dancing and the drink
findings.explanation: Garbled phrase: poison works through a person, not through 'the dancing and the drink'. Reads as a wording error.
findings.suggested_replacement: while the poison worked its way through Dusty's dancing

findings.exact_quote: Let me correct that formatting issue.
findings.explanation: Stray assistant meta-text at the end of the statement that would be read aloud to guests.

findings.exact_quote: I spent three years keeping this club's finances honest
findings.explanation: The introduction says Honey has done the accounts part-time for 'a couple of years', not three.
findings.suggested_replacement: I spent a couple of years keeping this club's finances honest

findings.exact_quote: If I wanted to protect myself, I'd have gone to Sandro first and laid it all out before Dusty could spin the story. That's what a person with nothing to hide does. That's what I did.
findings.explanation: Honey says she brought it privately to Dusty and Dusty then threatened to tell Sandro. Claiming she went to Sandro first contradicts that account.
findings.suggested_replacement: If I wanted to protect myself, I'd have gone to Sandro first and laid it all out before Dusty could spin the story. That's what a person with nothing to hide does.

findings.exact_quote: this memoir of hers
findings.explanation: Dusty is gender-neutral in this package, so 'hers' breaks the convention.
findings.suggested_replacement: this memoir of theirs

findings.exact_quote: things she shouldn't have been able to get her hands on
findings.explanation: Gendered pronouns used for the gender-neutral victim.
findings.suggested_replacement: things Dusty shouldn't have been able to get their hands on

findings.exact_quote: Did she ever let slip who else she was weaving into that little business scheme of hers?
findings.explanation: Repeated she/her for the gender-neutral victim.
findings.suggested_replacement: Did Dusty ever let slip who else they were weaving into that little business scheme of theirs?

findings.exact_quote: I told her then what I'll say now
findings.explanation: Victim referred to as 'her' despite being gender-neutral.
findings.suggested_replacement: I told Dusty then what I'll say now

findings.exact_quote: she was writing herself quite the chapter
findings.explanation: Gendered pronouns for the gender-neutral victim.
findings.suggested_replacement: they were writing themself quite the chapter

findings.exact_quote: making you feel like the only one who owed her something
findings.explanation: 'her' used for Dusty, who is gender-neutral.
findings.suggested_replacement: making you feel like the only one who owed them something

findings.exact_quote: So yes, I resented her.
findings.explanation: 'her' used for Dusty, who is gender-neutral.
findings.suggested_replacement: So yes, I resented Dusty.

findings.exact_quote: She mocked my gift
findings.explanation: Victim referred to with 'She' instead of Dusty or they.
findings.suggested_replacement: Dusty mocked my gift

findings.exact_quote: She was squeezing this entire club dry
findings.explanation: Gendered pronoun for the gender-neutral victim.
findings.suggested_replacement: Dusty was squeezing this entire club dry

findings.exact_quote: a willingness to watch her die on that floor surrounded by people who loved her
findings.explanation: 'her' used for the gender-neutral victim.
findings.suggested_replacement: a willingness to watch Dusty die on that floor surrounded by people who loved them

findings.exact_quote: I'll admit the bar got slow for a few minutes right around when the crowd surged toward the floor for the number.
findings.explanation: Says the bar got slow, yet the same passage has her three deep in orders and pouring as fast as she can. The next sentence says everyone wanted a Boogie Fever, so 'slow' contradicts it.
findings.suggested_replacement: I'll admit the bar got hectic for a few minutes right around when the crowd surged toward the floor for the number.

findings.exact_quote: don't forget Dusty herself wandered through half the club
findings.explanation: Dusty is gender-neutral in the package convention (master_context mixes pronouns), so "herself" is pronoun drift.
findings.suggested_replacement: don't forget Dusty themself wandered through half the club

findings.exact_quote: it's not short list.
findings.explanation: Missing article makes the sentence ungrammatical.
findings.suggested_replacement: it's not a short list.

findings.exact_quote: I didn't touch that drink last night, not once.
findings.explanation: The whole game takes place in one night, so "last night" is the wrong time reference for the night of the murder.
findings.suggested_replacement: I didn't touch that drink tonight, not once.

findings.exact_quote: than I ever did behind the bar that night
findings.explanation: Sandro is the club owner, not the bartender. Martha Gold works the bar, so placing him behind it contradicts his role and his own account of working the floor.
findings.suggested_replacement: than I ever did out on the floor that night

findings.exact_quote: I was dancing, same as I'm paid to do.
findings.explanation: Toni is a singer, not a dancer. Being paid to dance contradicts the speaker's own role, and Toni describes being paid to perform and sing elsewhere.
findings.suggested_replacement: I was singing along, same as I'm paid to do.

findings.exact_quote: A year of being the one bankrolling the place, quietly, gives a person access.
findings.explanation: Vera bankrolled Dusty's apartment, wardrobe and lifestyle, not the Golden Garter. Sandro owns the club and she did not fund it.
findings.suggested_replacement: A year of being the one bankrolling Dusty, quietly, gives a person access.
